findings.body:
**Persist newly created directory entries before reporting success.**

`apps/crq-python/review_ledger.py:306` can create `pending/` or `sha256/` on first use. Line 313 synchronizes only the leaf directory. Synchronizing a directory does not guarantee that its entry in its parent is durable. ([man7.org](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man2/fsync.2.html?utm_source=openai))

After a successful first `spool()` or `put()`, a system crash can therefore lose the directory and its accepted evidence. Synchronize each newly created directory’s parent before returning success. Apply the same directory-creation helper at Line 360.
findings.title: Persist newly created directory entries before reporting success.

findings.body:
**Require a creditable review for credited import results.**

`validate_sequence` records every review event in `reviews` (`review_ledger.py:275`). The import check at lines 290-292 accepts a `credited` result when its `review_id` appears in that map, without calling `creditable()`. A review that fails `creditable()` can therefore be linked from a `credited` import. The schema and `validate()` also accept this. `validate()` requires only a non-null `review_id` (lines 242-244). The ledger already requires `creditable()` for completed reviews (lines 225-226), so this check is a gap in the same invariant.

Credit calculations in `backfill_accounting.py` filter reviews with `creditable()` directly, so the inspected code does not add credit from this path. A consumer that trusts `result == "credited"` alone can count such a record.

Add a `creditable()` check to the `credited` branch. Raise `IntegrityError` when the linked review is not creditable. Check the `credited` fixture in `publisher_vector_emit_b1.py:481` before applying this change, because it links to `mid_review`, and its creditability was not inspected.
findings.title: Require a creditable review for credited import results.
